items.content_html:
WIP experimental patch; do not merge. This works fine from my testing, and doesn't immediately break anything important, but I imagine these two packages are in the same repository for a good reason, so splitting them like this is probably ill-advised. Still, every other distro does it through far worse methods.

This splits the 'kdePackages.kate' derivation into one derivation that builds 'kate' while patching out 'kwrite', and another that does the opposite. This reduces the overall closure size of either derivation, and allows us to follow in Fedora's footsteps and ship our Plasma module with only one text editor.

items.content_html:
Add module support for --stdin-from-command flag. I have made an assertion that the stdin backup is mutually exclusive with backing up from paths, but I still need to test that this is necessary - I initially thought it was but I'm not so sure now. I also made a few very small changes here and there in the nix code to make it look a little neater in my opinion.

I could potentially add support for the --stdin flag too, but this would require prepending the restic command with an external command and a pipe, which seems a bit messy - and the restic documentation says to prefer --stdin-from-command over --stdin anyway.

I could add an option for --stdin-filename, but I feel that this would be better for users to do in extraBackupArgs.

This is my first nixpkgs contribution so apologies if I've done anything wrong - please let me know!

TODO: still need to add release notes, and maybe add myself to maintainers (not sure about this?)

I'm trying to use the environmentFile option to set both the password and the repository, via the appropriate variables. Currently, the module disallows such behaviour, requiring either repository or repositoryFile, and passwordFile.

This is a minor change to tweak an assert and add null as a possible option to passwordFile. The module still checks if the environmentFile is set, and will throw an error appropriately.

items.content_html:
Description of changes

Adds nice and ionice support for restic. Inspired by:

  • https://restic.readthedocs.io/en/latest/faq.html#how-to-prioritize-restic-s-io-and-cpu-time
  • https://github.com/HubbeKing/restic-kubernetes/blob/master/backup.sh#L6

  • nixpkgs/nixos/modules/services/backup/btrbk.nix

    Lines 102 to 111 in 8610e08

    niceness = mkOption {
    description = lib.mdDoc "Niceness for local instances of btrbk. Also applies to remote ones connecting via ssh when positive.";
    type = types.ints.between (-20) 19;
    default = 10;
    };
    ioSchedulingClass = mkOption {
    description = lib.mdDoc "IO scheduling class for btrbk (see ionice(1) for a quick description). Applies to local instances, and remote ones connecting by ssh if set to idle.";
    type = types.enum [ "idle" "best-effort" "realtime" ];
    default = "best-effort";
    };

items.content_html:
Description of changes

Add a privateTmp setting copied over from a similar one in the borgbackup module. This allows to disable PrivateTmp (which implies PrivateMounts), and allows e.g. mounting and unmounting snapshots in the preStart/postStop scripts. PrivateMounts is annoying in that way:

File system namespaces are set up individually for each process forked off by the service manager. Mounts established in the namespace of the process created by ExecStartPre= will hence be cleaned up automatically as soon as that process exits and will not be available to subsequent processes forked off for ExecStart=

items.content_html:
The restic services module includes an option services.restic.backups.<name>.createWrapper that adds a shell wrapper around the restic binary that sets up environment variables for the given backup configuration.
This PR copies over the shell completion files from the standard restic binary to these new wrapper scripts, thus allowing shell completion for these wrapper scripts.

This implementation has not been extensively tested, as I am unfamiliar with shells outside of Bash.
The Bash shell completion has been tested and does work.
